_comment: Experiment dependency DAG for the CCS programme.
'depends_on' means: this experiment should not be run to confirmatory status
until the named nodes have read out, because its design or interpretation
'ccs_claim_gate' is separate: work may proceed, but the named condition must
hold before the node's results can license a CCS-level claim.
Stages are observed from the sibling repositories, not assigned from here.
'operator' uses COMMIT_INTERNAL / COMMIT_EXTERNAL as of 2026-09-03. Bare COMMIT is no longer a valid operator value.

nodes.question: Does the harness correctly compute retention matrices, forgetting, rollback and write accounting?
nodes.readout: Engineering validation passed. Promotion arm tied with replay; fixed-consolidation arm degenerate by construction. Explicitly not paper evidence.

nodes.question: Under matched budgets, does evidence-gated promotion across timescales improve the stability-plasticity trade-off for a frozen 0.5B language model?
nodes.gating_note: Still the programme's load-bearing node. main is unchanged at 3495d49 with an empty results/. Off-main branches carry an LM pilot that a sibling records as mechanically valid but scientifically uninterpretable (soft-prefix plastic representation underlearned), plus a predeclared LoRA representation-sufficiency repair and an Amendment F. None of that is merged and none of it is admissible.

nodes.question: Does the EXP-001 effect survive on established continual-learning benchmarks (CITB / TRACE)?
nodes.gating_note: Mandatory before any broad continual-learning claim, per the EXP-001 preregistration.

nodes.question: Does the strongest preregistered comparison replicate at ~7B?
nodes.gating_note: Scale replication only. Does not substitute for small-model ablations.

nodes.question: Does a consolidation threshold that adapts to observed stream statistics beat a threshold tuned once on development seeds, without using held-out signal?
nodes.gating_note: UMBRELLA-SIDE CANDIDATE, NOT THAT TRACK'S ROADMAP. state-promotion has not adopted an adaptive-threshold follow-on into its plan of record, and this node must not be read as though it had. It exists so that CCS-C5 - re-scoped on 2026-09-03 from adaptive-commitment to a COMMIT_INTERNAL follow-on - retains a mapped experiment rather than floating untestable. If that track declines it, the correct action is to retire CCS-C5, not to reassign it again.

nodes.question: Is the SDW-1 harness mechanically valid, and does the benchmark expose design defects before the protocol is frozen?
nodes.readout: DEV_CALIBRATION, trained and evaluated on development seeds {11,12,13}. All leakage gates L1-L7 pass, no ceiling or floor, optimal mapping is a bijection. Kill criterion K1 fired AGAINST the method: LEARNED - HEURISTIC = -0.0189, CI [-0.0235,-0.0104]. K2 did not fire: LEARNED - RANDOM_MATCHED = +0.1108, CI [+0.0927,+0.1264]. Declared not evidence.

nodes.question: Can a policy learn from delayed future task utility, under a unified resource budget, to allocate experience across substrates of differing persistence - and is any gain attributable to routing rather than capacity, compute, or privileged task identity?
nodes.gating_note: PROTOCOL v1.0 FROZEN 2026-09-03; blockers none; confirmatory seeds held out and NOT executed. That track's validator refuses to certify a confirmatory run whose commit, source-tree hash, config hash or seed does not match the lock, and any edit to src/, scripts/ or the frozen configuration invalidates it. 105 tests pass and the gating leakage suite passes; L5a is retained as permanently failed and non-gating, with the predeclared L5b cross-world attribution gate passing on one-shot audit seeds (Delta_real 0.4929 CI [0.4822, 0.5032]). THIS IS A VALIDITY AND PROTOCOL MILESTONE, NOT EMPIRICAL SUPPORT FOR CCS-C4. No confirmatory number exists. The track retains its deliberately low prior on the learned router beating the calibrated fixed heuristic. This synthetic freeze does NOT satisfy modular-consolidation's separate dependency, which requires an explicitly frozen or exported common LM/adaptation/routing substrate; verified 2026-09-03 that no such export exists and that EXP-002 remains BLOCKED.

nodes.question: Does the allocation result transfer to a language model?
nodes.gating_note: Declared BLOCKED by that track until the first mechanically valid state-promotion engineering pilot has been reviewed, so that shared two-timescale defects are not baked in.

nodes.question: Does a full module lifecycle beat a fixed bank of its own final size at identical capacity?
nodes.readout: Development toy. The fixed bank of the lifecycle's own final size beat the lifecycle by 7.8 points at identical capacity. Capacity explained the outcome. Not evidence about real models.

nodes.question: Is there an interior optimum in retention versus module capacity?
nodes.readout: Development simulator on a closed-form ridge learner. Retention versus capacity is monotone non-decreasing under any competent routing, across three independent mechanisms. Consequence drawn by that track: in the unbounded regime at matched capacity, consolidation has nothing to fix, and its only possible benefit is compression rather than forgetting. Not evidence about real models.

nodes.question: Under a hard capacity ceiling below the number of distinct skills, does freeing a slot by pooling retain more than freeing it by destroying or by refusing to admit?
nodes.readout: Development simulator, ceiling 3 with K*=6, 8 paired seeds at identical live-module count, parameters and storage. merge - evict = +0.204 retention, CI [+0.125,+0.296]. merge - deny = -0.017, CI spans zero, concealing plasticity +0.023 and forgetting +0.039 with CIs excluding zero. merge - random-merge = +0.009, CI spans zero. Not evidence about real models.

nodes.question: Does the binding-ceiling effect hold across ceiling phases under a frozen protocol?
nodes.readout: Executed as preregistered (prereg 74dc652 committed before runner 5b6314c) over the full frozen grid: K* in {6,12,24} x ceiling/K* in {1/6,1/3,1/2,2/3,5/6}, 8 development seeds 900-907, 5 arms, 600 rows, 2619 merge events. Construction VALID; capacity identical across arms within every cell. merge - evict is strongly positive everywhere non-degenerate (+0.16 to +0.29 retention, CI excludes zero). merge - deny changes SIGN with absolute K*, not with pressure: negative at every non-degenerate ratio for K*=6, positive from ratio 1/3 upward for K*=12 and K*=24. Within a K*, merge's advantage grows as the ceiling LOOSENS, and at the tightest ratio deny wins - the opposite of the motivating expectation. Merge criterion is no longer inert: at K*>=12, ratio >=1/3 it separates from random pairing on every event-level axis (precision 0.45-0.81 vs 0.07-0.19). DEVELOPMENT SEEDS ONLY; no confirmatory seed set has been drawn.
nodes.gating_note: Preregistration exists in that repository. Still a synthetic simulator; would not by itself license a real-model claim.
nodes.open_owner_decision: That track reports two readings of its own predeclared Pareto rule and declines to choose. Reading A (strict, as literally written) requires merge to dominate deny AND evict separately: no cell qualifies, verdict OPERATING_POINT. That track notes the clause is UNSATISFIABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, because B-EVICT-LRU installs a fresh module on every admission and so maximises plasticity by definition. Reading B (standard Pareto extension against the baseline set) finds a reproducible region: merge strictly dominates deny on both axes in 8 contiguous cells, replicated at two absolute K*. Both are computed over the complete grid and reported in analysis.json. Explicitly flagged as an owner decision. The umbrella does not resolve it and does not prefer a reading.

nodes.question: Do published modular continual-learning gains survive a budget-matched six-factor attribution lattice on real models?
nodes.gating_note: Preregistration is an explicit DRAFT and NOT FROZEN. Blocked until plasticity-routing freezes or exports the shared LM backbone, adapter family/rank, training budget and routing substrate. RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-03: plasticity-routing's Protocol v1.0 freeze covers its SYNTHETIC SDW-1 EXP-001 only; no LM substrate has been exported and its own EXP-002 language-model experiment remains BLOCKED. The blocker therefore stands. That track states explicitly that EXP-003 does not re-open EXP-100 by itself: D4 additionally requires a real-model result surviving capacity, storage and decision-compute accounting.

nodes.question: Does the harness run, do budgets bind, does audit separation hold, can every declared metric move, and does the benchmark sit between floor and ceiling?
nodes.readout: Single seed, no replication, no confidence intervals, generator still under construction. All four engineering objectives confirmed. Provisional orderings recorded: last-write-wins is hard to beat, and provenance-regrounding does not dominate on integrity despite winning on accuracy. Declared NOT EVIDENCE.

nodes.question: Does persistent state gradually depart from the evidence supposed to support it, and what does re-grounding cost at a matched ceiling?
nodes.ccs_claim_gate: state-promotion must establish an admissible substrate before any result here can license a CCS latent-architecture claim. That track declares itself architecture-agnostic and forbids such use of its results.
nodes.gating_note: Preregistered. Lifetime length is the independent variable; the pilot suggests mechanisms are near-indistinguishable at 8 epochs and separate at 128, which if it replicates would mean short-horizon evaluation misleads about mechanism choice.

nodes.question: When a late failure indicates one of several beliefs was wrong without saying which, can offline consolidation repair the culprit without corrupting the others?
nodes.gating_note: Five credit-assignment rules share one belief substrate so the rule is the only variable.

nodes.question: Does an integrated ACCUMULATE + ALLOCATE + COMMIT system beat the best single component under matched total budget?
nodes.gating_note: Deliberately left unresolved and undesigned. No host repository, and none is to be created yet: a dedicated integration repository becomes justified only once enough component mechanisms have admissible evidence to specify a non-arbitrary composition test. Designing it now would bake unsupported component choices into the synthesis programme. Its edges point at the confirmatory nodes it would need, not at the development calibrations that currently exist. As of 2026-09-03 cross-track budget harmonisation is an EXPLICIT PRECONDITION rather than an observation: 'matched total budget' is undefined until the resource envelope is populated, so the primary comparison cannot be stated, let alone run.
preconditions: ledger/resource_envelope.json maps every participating track's native accounting onto the common envelope, with no dimension left unmapped or marked incommensurable.
At least three component tracks hold admissible confirmatory evidence.
Integration gates I0-I2 in docs/INTEGRATION-CRITERIA.md are cleared.

nodes.question: Under streaming evidence, when should an agent choose among WAIT, THINK, ASK, RESPOND and ACT - trading accuracy against latency, compute, intervention cost, uncertainty, and consequence/reversibility?
nodes.gating_note: Repository still does not exist. Rewritten 2026-09-03: this track was previously recorded, incorrectly, as a refinement of state-promotion's memory-consolidation threshold. It is the outward/behavioural commitment track and was deliberately scoped separately from state-promotion. It is therefore NOT blocked on state-promotion/EXP-001. No CCS claim for behavioural commitment timing has been added yet, by owner decision: that claim is to be written only after this track's own literature audit and preregistration define its exact falsifiable form. Until then this node tests only CCS-C1, and adding a placeholder claim would be inventing a hypothesis on the track's behalf.

nodes.question: Can one learned commitment mechanism govern both when state is made durable and when an outward response is released, at least as well as two domain-specific mechanisms at matched total budget?
nodes.gating_note: No host repository and no design, like EXP-I1, and for the same reason: it cannot be specified until both domains have admissible mechanisms to unify. It is listed so that CCS-C12 has a mapped test and so the unification hypothesis stays visible as a claim rather than dissolving back into vocabulary. Note that it needs the resource envelope for the same reason EXP-I1 does: an internal write costs parameters and interference, an external action costs latency and consequence, and comparing them at 'matched total budget' presupposes an exchange rate that does not yet exist.
